newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gets National Australia Bank vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: HK gets National Australia Bank vote of confidence.

text.p: The National Australia Bank on Thursday gave a vote of confidence to Hong Kong and hinted it will be injecting funds into the territory imminently.
"We think the outlook for Hong Kong is good, we think it's good enough for us to make some commitments in the medium term," chief economist Alan Oster told a news conference in Hong Kong.

"I can't say anything beyond that, except watch this space next Tuesday when our bank would be announcing something in terms of an initiative in Hong Kong which implies basically that we're prepared to put funds into Hong Kong," he said.
National Australia Bank currently has a branch in Hong Kong.
Oster said the bank viewed the territory with optimism despite a recent slowdown in economic growth rates and a plunge in retail sales.
"We expect that consumption will start to pick up. Public investments in particular has been very strong and we think it will continue," he said.
On the Hong Kong dollar being pegged to the U.S. dollar, Oster said the local currency might be leaving itself open to fluctuations in the U.S. dollar.
